title: No internet access
symptoms: Several sites or applications fail on a training device.
questions: One device or many? Wired or wireless? When did it start? Does a local service work?
diagnostics: Check cable/link and Settings network status. Inspect IP, default gateway and DNS locally. Test only an authorized gateway; compare a known application.
observations: Disconnected link suggests a physical issue; a valid address alone does not prove connectivity. ICMP filtering can hide a working route.
causes: Loose cable, Wi-Fi disconnection, DHCP failure, gateway outage or upstream disruption.
resolution: With consent reconnect a loose lab cable or choose the approved Wi-Fi network. Retest the original application. Route shared outages to network support.
escalation: Multiple devices affected, no valid lease, or gateway unavailable after basic checks: network team.
record: Simulated scope, start time, link state, redacted findings, test outcome and escalation owner.

title: Connected to Wi-Fi but unable to open websites
symptoms: Wi-Fi shows connected but browser requests fail.
questions: All browsers and sites? Is a captive portal expected? Is a VPN required? Any certificate warning?
diagnostics: Inspect SSID and signal without sharing credentials. Check clock, IP/gateway and DNS. Open only the approved portal or known test page; compare another authorized application.
observations: Association to an access point does not imply internet access. Portal prompts, DNS errors and TLS warnings indicate different layers.
causes: Captive portal, resolver issue, incorrect clock, approved proxy/VPN problem or upstream outage.
resolution: Use the authorized captive portal. Correct clock only under policy. Ask network support to investigate proxy/VPN errors; never bypass certificate warnings.
escalation: Unexpected SSID/portal or certificate warning: security; shared loss of service: networking.
record: Simulated error wording, affected application types, signal quality, portal expectation and sanitized test results.

title: DNS resolution failures
symptoms: Hostname lookup fails or an application reports name resolution errors.
questions: One hostname or several? Other devices affected? Recent approved DNS or VPN change?
diagnostics: Use the lab DNS check or nslookup with an approved hostname. Inspect configured resolver locally. Compare expected records with the service owner.
observations: NXDOMAIN suggests no matching name; timeout suggests no timely answer. A successful lookup does not prove a web service works.
causes: Typo, missing record, unreachable resolver, stale cache or split DNS requiring VPN.
resolution: Correct a typed hostname. Follow approved VPN guidance. Cache flushing is a manual state change only when authorized and relevant; do not change DNS servers to bypass policy.
escalation: Repeated failure across devices or incorrect authoritative records: DNS/service owner.
record: Simulated error type, affected scope, expected versus observed response and owner; redact internal names.

title: Invalid or missing IP configuration
symptoms: No IPv4 address, unexpected subnet or 169.254.x.x with no expected route.
questions: DHCP expected? Is the link active? Is IPv6 working? Does another authorized device have the same problem?
diagnostics: Inspect ipconfig /all locally. Check link, DHCP enabled state, lease and default gateway. Do not infer outage solely from a link-local address.
observations: 169.254.x.x can indicate an absent IPv4 DHCP lease; IPv6 may still provide connectivity. Missing gateway affects off-subnet routing.
causes: DHCP unavailable, disconnected link, wrong VLAN or incorrect authorized static setup.
resolution: Restore an approved physical connection with consent. Request network support. Release/renew interrupts connectivity and is never automated by this lab.
escalation: DHCP/VLAN/static-address changes or repeated lease failures require network administrators.
record: Simulated DHCP state, link state, whether a gateway exists and sanitized lease observations; no MAC inventory.

title: Slow Windows computer
symptoms: Long sign-in, sluggish applications or sustained high resource usage.
questions: When did it start? One application or all? Recent updates? Is work saved? Any heat or disk warnings?
diagnostics: Observe Task Manager CPU, memory and disk over time. Check free storage and update status. Inspect only relevant Event Viewer summaries locally.
observations: Short resource spikes may be normal. Sustained pressure and reproducible delays provide stronger evidence; do not guess malware from CPU use alone.
causes: Resource pressure, pending updates, low storage, failing hardware or an application fault.
resolution: Save work and close an unneeded application with consent. Plan an approved restart or update window. Never end unknown system/security processes or delete user files.
escalation: Disk errors, repeated hangs, security alerts or persistent resource exhaustion: endpoint/hardware support.
record: Simulated duration, resource pattern, application version and sanitized event ID; no process dumps.

title: Application crashes
symptoms: An application closes unexpectedly or repeats an error.
questions: Which version and action trigger it? Is unsaved work at risk? One device or several?
diagnostics: Record sanitized error wording and time. Check Reliability Monitor or relevant Event Viewer entries. Reproduce only with dummy data after saving work.
observations: Consistent triggers suggest an application-specific issue; failures across applications may indicate wider endpoint trouble.
causes: Application defect, incompatible add-in, missing approved update or resource pressure.
resolution: Save work and restart the application with consent. Use approved updates or repair procedures through the software owner; preserve user data.
escalation: Repeated crash, data loss risk or repair requiring elevated rights: application/endpoint owner.
record: Simulated version, reproduction steps, sanitized error and event ID, impact and safe workaround.

title: Printer connectivity issues
symptoms: Jobs remain queued or an approved printer appears offline.
questions: One user or all? Correct printer selected? Any display error? Can the printer produce its own test page?
diagnostics: Inspect power, cable and printer status. View queue without reading document content. Compare an approved printer address and connectivity only if authorized.
observations: A device self-test separates printing hardware from workstation queue issues. Ping success alone does not validate the print service.
causes: Offline device, paper fault, wrong queue, driver issue or print server outage.
resolution: Select the approved queue or replenish paper with consent. Owner approval is required before cancelling jobs; do not restart a shared spooler automatically.
escalation: Shared queue failure, driver installation or persistent hardware fault: print support.
record: Simulated queue state, display error, affected scope and test outcome; omit document titles and contents.

title: Outlook synchronization problems
symptoms: Training mailbox appears stale or Outlook shows disconnected.
questions: Is connectivity working? One mailbox or many? Does authorized web access work? What sanitized error is shown?
diagnostics: Inspect Outlook connection/work-offline indicator and local clock. Compare approved web access. An authorized administrator may check Microsoft 365 service health.
observations: Web access working with desktop failure narrows the issue toward the client; shared failures may indicate a service incident.
causes: Offline mode, connectivity, expired authentication session, client issue or service outage.
resolution: After saving drafts, restart Outlook with consent; follow official sign-in prompts privately. Do not delete profiles, mail caches or messages as a first step.
escalation: Repeated authentication errors, shared outage or profile repair: Microsoft 365 support.
record: Simulated client version, connection indicator, sanitized error and comparison outcome; never include email contents or tokens.

title: Microsoft Teams audio or login issues
symptoms: Microphone not heard, wrong speaker selected or Teams sign-in fails.
questions: Audio or identity problem? Headset connected? One meeting or all? Is the approved account selected?
diagnostics: For audio inspect Teams device selection, mute state and Windows microphone permission; use a private test call when available. For login record sanitized error and check connectivity and clock.
observations: Wrong output device differs from network call quality problems; identity policy errors require authorized identity support.
causes: Incorrect audio device, denied microphone permission, connectivity or conditional access policy.
resolution: Select the intended headset and adjust only the necessary approved permission with consent. Use official authentication privately; never request passwords or MFA codes.
escalation: Persistent login/policy failure: identity team; repeated audio device fault: endpoint support.
record: Simulated audio path, app version, permission state and sanitized error; no meeting recordings or participant data.

title: OneDrive synchronization problems
symptoms: Sync icon shows paused, pending or a conflict.
questions: Which sync indicator appears? Is storage full? Is the affected file open? Is connectivity available?
diagnostics: Inspect the sync indicator and sanitized error. Check available local/cloud storage through authorized views without opening private documents.
observations: Paused sync, capacity errors and file conflicts require different actions. A local file is not proof that a cloud copy is current.
causes: Paused client, low storage, unsupported filename, open file or conflicting edits.
resolution: Resume an intentionally paused client with consent. Preserve both conflict copies and ask the data owner to reconcile them. Do not delete local/cloud folders or reset/unlink automatically.
escalation: Data integrity risk, permissions issue or persistent sync failure: storage/Microsoft 365 owner.
record: Simulated sync status, error category and scope; omit filenames, personal paths and document contents.

title: Account lockout
symptoms: A fictional account sign-in explicitly reports locked access.
questions: What is the sanitized error? When did it start? Is there a recent password change or suspected unexpected activity? Never ask for the password.
diagnostics: Stop repeated sign-in attempts. Follow approved identity verification and escalation policy; no directory queries are performed in this lab.
observations: Lockout differs from disabled account, expired password and conditional access denial. Only authorized identity staff can confirm the actual account state.
causes: Repeated failures, stale saved credentials or potentially malicious attempts; these remain hypotheses until investigated.
resolution: Refer to the authorized identity team for verified recovery under policy. Never unlock or reset accounts in this lab or ask users to send MFA codes.
escalation: Identity team for recovery; security team for suspicious attempts or unexpected MFA requests.
record: Simulated start time, sanitized error, impact and escalation decision; no usernames, identity documents or credentials.

title: Suspicious email or phishing report
symptoms: Unexpected request for credentials, payment or opening a suspicious attachment.
questions: Was anything opened or entered? Is there an unexpected MFA prompt? Ask for a sanitized description, never passwords or message contents in this lab.
diagnostics: Do not click links, open attachments, reply or contact the sender. Use the approved reporting mechanism; do not upload messages to public analysis sites.
observations: Urgency, impersonation and unexpected links are warning signs, not proof by themselves. Trained security staff assess the original evidence in approved systems.
causes: Potential phishing, impersonation or legitimate but unexpected correspondence.
resolution: Report via the authorized security workflow. If interaction occurred, stop further activity and contact security immediately; follow their containment instructions.
escalation: Immediate security escalation after credential entry, attachment execution, financial request or suspicious MFA.
record: Simulated interaction type, time and escalation owner; preserve actual evidence only through approved security channels, never in this lab.
